about: Mini-stories for Story Order, written for this app at about a 2nd to 3rd grade reading level. Each story has a title and 4 sentences in the order they happen. Every story must have only one sensible order. Characters are made up.

stories.title: The Lost Kite
sentences: Mia flew her red kite at the park.
A strong wind pulled the string from her hand.
The kite got stuck in a tall tree.
Her dad used a ladder to get it down.

stories.title: Fresh Bread
sentences: Sam mixed flour, water, and yeast.
He let the dough rise for an hour.
Then he baked it in the hot oven.
The warm bread smelled so good!

stories.title: The Bean Seed
sentences: Lee planted a bean seed in a cup.
She gave it water every day.
A tiny green sprout popped up.
Soon the plant was taller than the cup.

stories.title: Snow Day
sentences: Snow fell all night long.
In the morning, the yard was white.
The kids rolled three big snowballs.
They stacked them to make a snowman.

stories.title: From Egg to Frog
sentences: A frog laid eggs in the pond.
The eggs hatched into tadpoles.
The tadpoles slowly grew legs.
They hopped out as little frogs.

stories.title: The Wiggly Tooth
sentences: Ben's front tooth felt wiggly.
He bit into a crunchy apple.
The tooth fell right out!
He put it under his pillow that night.

stories.title: Party Time
sentences: Ava made a list of friends to invite.
She mailed the party cards.
Her friends came over on Saturday.
Everyone sang and ate cake.

stories.title: Puddle Jumping
sentences: Dark clouds filled the sky.
Big drops of rain began to fall.
Max opened his yellow umbrella.
He jumped in every puddle on the way home.

stories.title: The Shark Book
sentences: Zoe found a book about sharks.
She checked it out at the front desk.
She read it every night that week.
Then she took it back to the library.

stories.title: A New Butterfly
sentences: A caterpillar ate leaf after leaf.
It grew fat and long.
It made a hard shell called a chrysalis.
Two weeks later, a butterfly came out.

stories.title: Pancake Morning
sentences: Dad cracked two eggs into a bowl.
He stirred in milk and flour.
He poured the batter into a hot pan.
We ate the pancakes with syrup.

stories.title: Game Day
sentences: The team put on their blue shirts.
The game started with a big kick.
Nora scored a goal at the very end.
The whole team cheered for her.

stories.title: Muddy Puppy
sentences: The puppy rolled in the mud.
Now he was brown and messy.
Eli gave him a bubbly bath.
The puppy shook water all over Eli!

stories.title: Blanket Fort
sentences: Jay pulled the cushions off the couch.
He leaned them against two chairs.
He laid a blanket over the top.
Then he crawled inside his new fort.

stories.title: Homemade Ice Pop
sentences: Kim poured juice into a small cup.
She put a stick in the middle.
She set the cup in the freezer.
The next day she had an ice pop.

stories.title: Duck Pond Ride
sentences: Omar put on his bike helmet.
He rode his bike to the lake.
He stopped to watch the ducks swim.
Then he rode back home for lunch.

stories.title: The Sandcastle
sentences: Rosa filled her bucket with wet sand.
She flipped it over to make a tower.
She built a wall around the tower.
A big wave washed it all away.

stories.title: Lemonade Stand
sentences: Tom squeezed six lemons.
He mixed the juice with water and sugar.
He set up a stand by the sidewalk.
He sold ten cups by noon.

stories.title: Ant Picnic
sentences: The family spread a blanket on the grass.
They set out sandwiches and grapes.
A line of ants marched toward the food.
They packed up and ate inside instead.

stories.title: Lights Out
sentences: Lightning flashed across the sky.
The lights in the house went out.
Grandma lit a candle.
We told stories until the power came back.

stories.title: Robin's Nest
sentences: A robin gathered twigs and grass.
She built a nest in the tree.
She laid three blue eggs.
Soon, baby birds were chirping for food.

stories.title: The Lost Mitten
sentences: Leo wore his green mittens to school.
At recess, one mitten fell in the snow.
His friend found it by the slide.
Leo thanked her with a big smile.

stories.title: Blue Sky Picture
sentences: Ella put on an old shirt to paint.
She dipped her brush in blue paint.
She painted a sky over a little house.
She hung her picture on the fridge.

stories.title: Lunch Time
sentences: Get out two slices of bread.
Spread cheese on one slice.
Add ham on top of the cheese.
Press the slices together and take a bite.

stories.title: Apple Pie
sentences: We drove to the apple farm.
We picked a basket of red apples.
At home, Mom peeled and sliced them.
Soon an apple pie was baking.

stories.title: Bubbles the Goldfish
sentences: Ivy bought a goldfish at the pet store.
She carried it home in a plastic bag.
She let it swim into its new tank.
She named the fish Bubbles.

stories.title: Noodle Night
sentences: Dad filled a big pot with water.
Small bubbles formed on the bottom.
Soon the water was boiling.
Dad added the noodles.

stories.title: Starry Night
sentences: The sun set behind the hills.
The sky turned pink, then dark blue.
One by one, the stars came out.
We found the Big Dipper.

stories.title: Spelling Test
sentences: The teacher gave the class ten new words.
Ana practiced them every night.
On Friday, the class took the test.
Ana spelled all ten words right!

stories.title: Where Is Rex?
sentences: The gate was left open.
Rex ran out to chase a squirrel.
The family searched the whole street.
They found Rex napping on a porch.

stories.title: On the Ice
sentences: Lily laced up her new skates.
She stepped onto the ice.
She wobbled and fell down.
She got up and tried again.

stories.title: Sled Hill
sentences: Gus pulled his sled up the hill.
He sat down and held on tight.
The sled zoomed to the bottom.
He climbed back up to go again.

stories.title: Tomato Garden
sentences: In spring, Nana planted tomato seeds.
All summer, the vines grew tall.
Green tomatoes turned bright red.
In the fall, she picked a big basket.

stories.title: Popcorn
sentences: Pour the kernels into the pot.
Put on the lid and turn up the heat.
Listen for the pop, pop, pop!
Shake on some salt and enjoy.

stories.title: A Letter for Grandpa
sentences: Nick wrote a letter to his grandpa.
He put it in an envelope with a stamp.
The mail carrier picked it up.
Three days later, Grandpa read it.

stories.title: Sick Day
sentences: Maya woke up with a sore throat.
Her mom took her temperature.
The doctor said to rest and drink water.
In two days, Maya felt better.

stories.title: The Melting Ice Cube
sentences: Ty left an ice cube on the table.
The sun shone through the window.
The ice cube started to shrink.
Soon there was only a puddle.

stories.title: Fire Trucks
sentences: Smoke rose from the old barn.
A farmer called for help.
Fire trucks raced down the road.
Firefighters sprayed water on the flames.

stories.title: Train Ride
sentences: We bought tickets at the station.
The train pulled in with a whistle.
We found two seats by the window.
We watched the fields rush past.

stories.title: The Spider's Web
sentences: A spider spun a thread from a branch.
It wove a big round web.
A fly buzzed into the sticky web.
The spider had its lunch.

stories.title: Pumpkin Face
sentences: Priya picked the biggest pumpkin in the patch.
At home, she cut off the top and scooped it out.
Then she carved two eyes and a big smile.
That night, a candle made the face glow.

stories.title: Clean Room
sentences: Kofi's toys covered his whole bedroom floor.
First, he put the blocks back in their bin.
Then he lined his books up on the shelf.
At last, he could see the floor again!

stories.title: Goodbye, Snowman
sentences: The sun came out the day after the snowstorm.
Our snowman's carrot nose fell to the ground.
By lunch, he was only half as tall.
By evening, only his hat sat in a puddle.

stories.title: The Hen's Egg
sentences: A hen sat on her egg for three weeks.
One morning, the egg began to crack.
A wet little chick wiggled out.
By noon, its feathers were dry and fluffy.

stories.title: Paper Airplane
sentences: Diego folded a sheet of paper in half.
He folded the corners down to make wings.
He threw the plane across the yard.
It glided all the way to the fence!

stories.title: No More Training Wheels
sentences: Dad took the training wheels off Aisha's bike.
He held the seat as she started to pedal.
Then he let go without telling her.
Aisha rode down the whole block alone!

stories.title: The Loose Button
sentences: A button popped off Grandpa's coat.
Grandma threaded a needle with black thread.
She sewed the button back in place.
Grandpa buttoned his coat and went outside.

stories.title: After the Rain
sentences: Rain tapped on the window all morning.
After lunch, the rain finally stopped.
The sun peeked out from behind a cloud.
A bright rainbow stretched over the hills.

stories.title: Car Wash
sentences: Hana and her dad filled a bucket with soap.
They scrubbed the dusty car with big sponges.
Then they sprayed off the bubbles with the hose.
The clean car shined in the sun.

stories.title: A Card of My Own
sentences: Felix filled out a form at the library desk.
The librarian printed his very own card.
He picked out three books about trains.
He used his new card to check them out.

stories.title: The Class Tree
sentences: The class dug a deep hole by the playground.
They set a small tree in the hole.
They filled the hole back in with dirt.
Then each kid poured in a cup of water.

stories.title: Hot Cocoa
sentences: Mom warmed a pot of milk on the stove.
She stirred in cocoa powder and sugar.
She poured the cocoa into two mugs.
We dropped marshmallows on top and sipped.

stories.title: The Leaf Pile
sentences: Red and yellow leaves covered the yard.
Raj raked them into one huge pile.
He took a running start and jumped in.
Leaves flew everywhere, so he raked again.

stories.title: Time for a Haircut
sentences: Sofia's bangs hung down over her eyes.
She sat in the tall chair at the barber shop.
Snip, snip went the scissors.
Now she could see the mirror again!

stories.title: The Bird Feeder
sentences: Theo filled a feeder with sunflower seeds.
He hung it on a branch outside the window.
The next day, a red bird landed on it.
Soon five birds were eating the seeds.

stories.title: New School
sentences: Lucy packed pencils and a notebook in her bag.
In the morning, she rode the bus to school.
Her new teacher showed her to her desk.
By recess, she had made a new friend.

stories.title: Ball on the Roof
sentences: Kai kicked the ball high into the air.
It landed on top of the garage roof.
His big sister climbed a ladder to reach it.
She tossed it down, and the game went on.

stories.title: Dish Duty
sentences: After dinner, Ming filled the sink with suds.
She scrubbed each plate with a sponge.
She rinsed the plates in clean water.
Then she stacked them on the rack to dry.

stories.title: Pond in Winter
sentences: In fall, the pond water was cool.
In early winter, thin ice formed on top.
By January, the ice was thick and hard.
In spring, the ice melted and ducks came back.

stories.title: Clay Volcano
sentences: Ruby built a little volcano out of clay.
She poured baking soda into the top.
Then she added a splash of vinegar.
Red foam bubbled out and ran down the sides!

stories.title: The Birdhouse
sentences: Grandpa cut four boards for a birdhouse.
Ines nailed the walls together.
Then they added a slanted roof on top.
They hung it up and waited for a bird.

stories.title: Puppy School
sentences: Yuki held a treat above her puppy's nose.
She said, "Sit!" in a clear voice.
The puppy sat down on the grass.
Yuki gave him the treat and a pat.

stories.title: Home Run
sentences: The pitcher threw the ball over the plate.
Marco swung his bat with all his might.
Crack! The ball flew over the fence.
Marco ran around all the bases.

stories.title: Kitten Grows Up
sentences: The kitten was born with its eyes shut tight.
After ten days, its eyes opened.
Soon it could wobble around on four legs.
By summer, it was a big cat chasing yarn.

stories.title: Strawberry Snack
sentences: Nadia washed the strawberries in the sink.
She cut off the green tops.
She sliced each berry in half.
She mixed them with yogurt for a snack.

stories.title: Up the Mountain
sentences: We packed water and snacks for the hike.
We walked up a long, rocky trail.
At the top, we could see the whole valley.
We ate our snacks and then hiked down.

stories.title: Night in a Tent
sentences: Jonah and his mom found a flat spot in the woods.
They set up the tent and staked it down.
That night, they roasted marshmallows.
Then they zipped into their sleeping bags.

stories.title: Drippy Cone
sentences: Lena got a scoop of ice cream on a cone.
It was a hot day, so it began to melt.
A sticky drip ran down onto her fingers.
She licked fast to catch the next drip.

stories.title: Ollie's Shadow
sentences: In the morning, Ollie's shadow was very long.
At noon, the sun was high and his shadow tiny.
In the evening, his shadow grew long again.
Then the sun set and his shadow was gone.

stories.title: Making the Bed
sentences: Ari pulled the sheet smooth across the bed.
He spread the blanket over the sheet.
He fluffed his pillow and set it at the top.
Last, he sat his teddy bear on the pillow.

stories.title: Flat Tire
sentences: Zara's bike tire went flat near the park.
She walked the bike back home.
Her uncle helped her patch the hole.
Then they pumped the tire full of air.

stories.title: Moving Day
sentences: Movers carried boxes onto a big truck.
The truck drove to the new house.
The family unpacked the boxes one by one.
That night, Pablo slept in his new room.

stories.title: Blowing Bubbles
sentences: Nina was scared to put her face in the pool.
Her teacher showed her how to blow bubbles.
She practiced blowing bubbles every week.
By summer's end, she could swim the pool.

stories.title: Crunchy Carrots
sentences: In spring, Abu planted carrot seeds in rows.
Thin green tops poked out of the dirt.
In summer, he pulled up a long orange carrot.
He washed it off and crunched it for a snack.

stories.title: Peanut the Hamster
sentences: The class got a hamster named Peanut.
Each child took a turn feeding him.
On Friday, Luca took Peanut home.
On Monday, he brought Peanut back to class.

stories.title: Puzzle Time
sentences: Grandma dumped the puzzle pieces on the table.
First, we found all the edge pieces.
We put them together to make a frame.
Then we filled in the middle until it was done.

stories.title: Spring Lambs
sentences: In early spring, a sheep had twin lambs.
The lambs stood up on wobbly legs.
They drank milk from their mother.
A week later, they were hopping in the field.

stories.title: Bake Sale
sentences: The class baked cookies for a bake sale.
They wrapped each cookie in a small bag.
On Saturday, they sold cookies at school.
They used the money to buy new books.

stories.title: Brush, Brush, Brush
sentences: Wet your toothbrush under the tap.
Squeeze on a dab of toothpaste.
Brush every tooth for two minutes.
Rinse your mouth and spit in the sink.

stories.title: The Pink Shell
sentences: Mei walked along the beach at low tide.
She spotted a pink shell in the sand.
She rinsed it off in a tide pool.
At home, she set it on her shelf.

stories.title: Jump Rope
sentences: Tess could only jump rope three times in a row.
She practiced in the driveway every day.
After a week, she could jump twenty times.
At recess, she showed her whole class.

stories.title: Shake Up Some Butter
sentences: Pour cream into a jar and close the lid.
Shake the jar hard for ten minutes.
A lump of yellow butter forms inside.
Spread the butter on warm toast.

stories.title: Laundry Line
sentences: Grandma took the wet clothes out of the washer.
She hung them on the line with clothespins.
The wind and sun dried them by noon.
We folded them and put them away.

stories.title: Shoes That Fit
sentences: Elsa's shoes were too tight on her toes.
She went to the shoe store with her mom.
She tried on three pairs of shoes.
She chose the blue pair that fit just right.

stories.title: The Lion Part
sentences: Mateo got the part of the lion in the class play.
He practiced his lines every night.
On the big night, he roared on stage.
Everyone in the crowd clapped and cheered.

stories.title: Busy Bee
sentences: A bee landed on a yellow flower.
It filled up on sweet nectar.
Then it flew home to the hive.
There the bees turned the nectar into honey.

stories.title: Swish!
sentences: Jin dribbled the ball down the court.
He stopped and aimed at the hoop.
He jumped and let the ball go.
Swish! It dropped right through the net.

stories.title: Dumpling Night
sentences: Grandma rolled the dough into small circles.
Wei put a spoonful of filling on each one.
They pinched the edges closed.
Then they steamed the dumplings for dinner.

stories.title: A Full Saturday
sentences: In the morning, Amara had soccer practice.
At lunch, she ate a picnic at the park.
In the afternoon, she helped wash the dog.
That night, she fell asleep right away.

stories.title: Avocado Pit
sentences: Selma poked toothpicks into an avocado pit.
She set it on top of a glass of water.
Weeks later, a root grew down into the water.
Then a green stem grew up from the top.

stories.title: Block Tower
sentences: Ezra stacked blocks into a tall tower.
His baby sister crawled over to see it.
She bumped it with her hand.
The tower crashed, and they both laughed.

stories.title: Blueberry Muffins
sentences: Ama took a pail to the blueberry bushes.
She picked berries until the pail was full.
At home, Mom baked them into muffins.
They ate warm muffins for breakfast.

stories.title: A Tug on the Line
sentences: Grandpa put a worm on Finn's hook.
Finn cast his line into the lake.
Soon the line gave a hard tug.
He reeled in a small fish and let it go.

stories.title: The Maple Tree's Year
sentences: In spring, the maple tree grew tiny buds.
In summer, its leaves were big and green.
In fall, its leaves turned red and dropped.
In winter, its bare branches held snow.

stories.title: Taco Night
sentences: Dad warmed the taco shells in the oven.
Lupe filled each shell with beans.
She piled lettuce and cheese on top.
Then the family crunched into their tacos.

stories.title: The Big Race
sentences: The runners lined up at the start.
The coach blew a whistle.
Kemal ran as fast as he could.
He crossed the finish line out of breath.

stories.title: Tulip Bulbs
sentences: In the fall, Iris planted tulip bulbs.
All winter, the bulbs slept under the snow.
In spring, green shoots poked up.
Soon, red tulips bloomed by the door.

stories.title: Recycling Day
sentences: Pia rinsed out the empty cans and jars.
She sorted them into the blue bin.
She rolled the bin out to the curb.
In the morning, the truck emptied it.

stories.title: Wrapping a Gift
sentences: Tariq put a toy car in a box.
He wrapped the box in shiny paper.
He tied a bow on top.
At the party, his friend tore off the paper.

stories.title: Clay Bowl
sentences: Gia shaped a lump of clay into a bowl.
She let it dry for two days.
Then she painted it bright green.
Now she keeps her hair clips in it.

stories.title: Farm Field Trip
sentences: The class rode a bus to the farm.
The farmer showed them how to milk a cow.
Each kid got a turn to try.
On the ride back, everyone talked about cows.

stories.title: Spilled Milk
sentences: Amir reached across the table for the bread.
His elbow knocked over his glass of milk.
Milk spread across the table.
He grabbed a towel and wiped it up.

stories.title: Sprinkler Fun
sentences: It was the hottest day of summer.
Dad set up the sprinkler on the lawn.
The kids ran squealing through the cold water.
Then they lay on towels to dry in the sun.

stories.title: Rocket Launch
sentences: Hugo pumped air into his toy rocket.
He counted down from three to one.
The rocket shot high into the sky.
It floated back down on a little parachute.

stories.title: Chicken Soup
sentences: Grandpa chopped carrots and celery.
He dropped them into a pot of broth.
The soup bubbled on the stove for an hour.
He ladled it into bowls for everyone.

stories.title: Tie Your Shoes
sentences: Cross the two laces to make an X.
Tuck one lace under and pull tight.
Make a loop and wrap the other lace around it.
Push that lace through to make a bow.

stories.title: Turtle Beach
sentences: A sea turtle crawled up onto the beach.
She dug a hole and laid her eggs.
Weeks later, tiny turtles hatched.
They scurried across the sand to the sea.

stories.title: Painting the Fence
sentences: The old fence was peeling and gray.
Aditi and her mom scraped off the old paint.
They brushed on a coat of white paint.
By evening, the fence looked brand new.

stories.title: Frosting the Cake
sentences: Juno baked a round cake for her dad.
She let it cool on the counter.
She spread chocolate frosting over the top.
Then she pressed candles into the frosting.

stories.title: Snow Angel
sentences: Fresh snow covered the backyard.
Asha lay down on her back in the snow.
She swept her arms and legs back and forth.
She stood up and saw a snow angel.

stories.title: Morning Rush
sentences: Owen's alarm buzzed at seven o'clock.
He got dressed and ate his cereal.
He grabbed his backpack by the door.
He ran out just as the bus pulled up.

stories.title: Making Green
sentences: Remy squeezed blue paint onto a plate.
Next to it, he squeezed some yellow paint.
He mixed the two colors with his brush.
The paint turned bright green!

stories.title: Island Lunch
sentences: Grandpa pushed the rowboat into the lake.
Mira climbed in and sat in the middle.
Grandpa rowed them out to a little island.
They ate lunch there and then rowed back.

stories.title: Firefly Jar
sentences: At dusk, tiny lights blinked in the grass.
Cyrus caught a firefly in a jar.
He watched it glow on and off.
Then he opened the jar and let it fly away.

stories.title: The Missing Wheel
sentences: One wheel fell off Tomas's toy truck.
He found the wheel under the couch.
His mom helped him snap it back on.
He raced the truck across the kitchen floor.

stories.title: Grocery Trip
sentences: Malik and his dad wrote a shopping list.
At the store, they filled the cart.
They paid at the checkout.
At home, they put the food away.

stories.title: Pizza Night
sentences: Spread the dough into a big circle.
Spoon tomato sauce over the dough.
Sprinkle cheese on top of the sauce.
Bake it until the cheese bubbles.

stories.title: A Scarf for Winter
sentences: Grandma taught Ilse how to knit.
Ilse knit a few rows every night.
After a month, the scarf was long enough.
She wore it on the first cold day.

stories.title: Giant Bubble
sentences: Dev mixed soap and water in a bowl.
He dipped a wand into the soapy mix.
He blew gently through the ring.
A big bubble floated over the fence.

stories.title: The Snowplow
sentences: Snow piled high on the road overnight.
A snowplow rumbled by at dawn.
It pushed the snow to the side of the road.
Now the school bus could get through.
